text: You're at a restaurant, hungry and ready. The menu arrives, a world of delicious choices. But a subtle overwhelm creeps in.
Your eyes dart across prices and dishes. You want a tasty meal, good value, but finding it feels like a puzzle.
You might avoid the priciest item, or pick something mid-range. You think you’re making a smart choice on your own.
But these menus are engineered. Restaurants strategically place decoys and high-profit dishes, guiding your eye exactly where they want.
That super expensive item acts as an anchor, making the slightly cheaper option next to it seem like a great deal. Your choice was subtly nudged.
Next time you pick up a menu, you’ll see past the names and prices. You’ll spot the invisible system, becoming a more intentional diner.
